title: Liquidity-Squeeze / Risk-Off: Correlations Going to 1 and What Hedges Actually Hold
content: During acute liquidity-squeeze episodes (2008 GFC, March 2020), forced deleveraging drives indiscriminate asset sales across risk classes, causing cross-asset correlations to spike sharply toward 1 as managers sell whatever is liquid to meet margin calls — including gold, which paradoxically falls in the first wave before recovering. The most reliable immediate hedges are long-volatility structures (VIX calls returned approximately 163x in 2008 and 127x in March 2020 at peak) and long USD, as dollar demand surges when global collateral chains seize. Short-dated US Treasuries and JPY/CHF also historically hold or appreciate in pure risk-off / deflation-shock regimes, but the 2022 inflation-driven tightening cycle proved a critical exception: the SPX-AGG correlation flipped to +0.50, the highest on record, meaning the bond hedge failed precisely when equities fell. The practical regime rule is: in a liquidity-squeeze, pay the vol premium continuously and hold the reserve currency; do not rely on gold or nominal duration as first-response hedges until the acute deleveraging phase clears.
lesson: Long-vol (VIX calls) and long-USD are the only hedges with a demonstrated track record of holding through the acute deleveraging phase of a liquidity squeeze; gold and duration only serve as hedges after the first margin-call wave clears, and duration fails entirely in inflation-driven tightening regimes.
